understanding: HashiCorp Raft is a Go replicated-log library with follower, candidate, and leader execution loops. Leaders persist log entries locally, replicate them through an injected Transport, advance commitment, and apply committed entries through an FSM. Followers validate AppendEntries prefixes, truncate conflicting suffixes, persist received entries, update commit/application state, and can install snapshots. Configuration entries are represented in the log and tracked separately as committed/latest configurations. StableStore, LogStore, SnapshotStore, Transport, and FSM are injected interfaces; concrete backend behavior and schedule control are not established by the supplied materials.

activities.purpose: Form, persist, replicate, and advance replicated log decisions and commitment.
activities.realization_summary: Leader dispatchLogs assigns index and term, stores entries locally, records local replication, and notifies per-peer replication routines. activities.purpose: Acquire, change, lose, and interpret Raft authority and term context.
activities.realization_summary: The main loop selects follower, candidate, or leader behavior. Follower heartbeat expiry can enter candidate state; candidates perform pre-vote or vote collection; incoming AppendEntries or vote requests with newer terms update term and may force follower state. Leaders step down on relevant signals and resolve in-flight operations with leadership-loss errors.

activities.purpose: Restore lagging, restarted, disconnected, or snapshot-requiring participants to legal participation.
activities.realization_summary: A leader falls back to the latest stored snapshot when a follower is too far behind retained logs. activities.purpose: Create, encode, persist, commit, activate, and consume participant configuration versions.
activities.realization_summary: Configuration changes derive a new configuration from the latest configuration, validate unique IDs and addresses and at least one voter, encode a compatibility-specific log entry, dispatch it, update latest configuration state, and restart peer replication. Received configuration entries update committed/latest configuration tracking. At most one uncommitted configuration is represented by the tracked state.

activities.purpose: Turn committed log decisions into FSM state-machine effects and client-visible responses.
activities.realization_summary: processLogs skips already-applied indices, loads committed entries from futures or LogStore, filters non-FSM log types, batches applicable entries, sends them to the FSM mutation channel, and updates last-applied state. FSM.Apply or optional ApplyBatch produces response values returned through futures. Barriers are sent to the FSM; no-ops and some configuration entries are filtered.

activities.purpose: Persist, publish, compact, delete, and reconstruct protocol history and recovery evidence.
activities.realization_summary: Leaders and followers write logs through LogStore. Snapshot execution obtains FSM state, captures committed configuration metadata, creates and persists a snapshot, closes it, records last-snapshot metadata, and deletes old logs while retaining configured trailing logs. Snapshot creation is blocked when the FSM-applied index is behind the committed configuration index.

activities.purpose: Admit client operations, report leadership and commit outcomes, and expose applied or rejected work.
activities.realization_summary: Follower paths reject leader-only requests with ErrNotLeader. Leader setup dispatches client logs and responds to in-flight futures on leadership loss, restore supersession, shutdown, or persistence errors. Apply and Barrier semantics distinguish committed log processing from FSM application, but the complete public API and future lifecycle are not supplied.
